turn_text: The earned income tax credit is a raise for ordinary working Americans. Any family making under $75,000 a year would, under this proposal, get a refund at the end of the year up to $10,000. It would be a pay raise for nurses, teachers, firefighters, machinists, drywallers, people who are in the middle class or working Americans. And the idea is it would make up for the stagnation of wages for the 50% of American workers whose wages have stagnated since 1980.

And the earned income tax credit isn't a new tax credit. So are you just, would your proposal basically expand and increase the amount of money that people would get as a result of being eligible for this?

Exactly. The Earned Income Tax Credit was a conservative idea. It was an idea proposed by Milton Friedman and had support of economists, both conservative and liberal economists. And currently it is one of the most successful programs in the government and it helps the working poor. The people who are probably making up to $30, $35,000 qualify for the Earned Income Tax Credit. And it does two things. It's pro-work because it gets more people joining the labor force and it gets more employers hiring because the employers know that their employee is going to get a wage supplement.

Now, the question is, I'm sure for a family that's making $75,000 a year, a tax credit of $10,000 is significant, but wouldn't it also be significant if Americans across the board got a wage increase? I think there are still people who are fighting for $15 an hour. It just seems as you mentioned earlier, this is one solution to wage stagnation, but how do we move past that? This just seems like it's one solution to a bigger problem.

You're absolutely right. In fact, I would argue it has to be coupled with a $15 minimum wage increase. Otherwise, if you just have an Earn Income Tax Credit without a minimum wage increase, then some of the Earn Income Tax Credit could go to the employer because the employer will say, OK, this employee is getting a wage subsidy from the government, I don't need to pay them as much. And the most successful Earn Income Tax Credits are combined with increasing the minimum wage. That ensures that it is really the worker that is benefiting from the Earn Income Tax Credit.
